chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, who said:

I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the bleacher and the jeweller, are they liable? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The people would not be straightened unless they are made to be liable.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And Yunus used to work by it and seize (by it – holding people liable)'.

key_terms.الْقَصَّارِ: Bleacher (one who cleans and whitens wool/cloth)
key_terms.يَأْخُذُ: Seizes/Takes (implies enforcing the liability or taking compensation)

ai.seo_question: Are craftsmen like jewelers and bleachers legally liable for defects in their work according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the principle of *daman* (liability) is extended to artisans like bleachers and jewelers, emphasizing that holding them accountable ensures quality and fairness in commercial transactions. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on professional responsibility as a means of maintaining social equity, a principle actively practiced by the narrator Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman.
